title: Grateful Dead Live at Civic Auditorium on 1970-03-07

ai_review.summary: Fair‑quality audience tape captures a fiery 1970 performance highlighted by an epic China > Rider > High Time and soaring Lovelight.
ai_review.review: Despite the lo‑fi, crackly AUD source, this show shines with high energy and tight playing. Reviewers rave about the Black Peter opening, the blistering China > Rider > High Time sequence, a monster The Other One, and an unforgettable 25‑minute Lovelight, while noting pops, hiss and occasional pitch issues that keep it from being pristine.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars for the performance; recording quality is consistently described as average/fair but still listenable, yielding a strong overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crackles, hiss, occasional pops and splices; some reviewers note pitch being too sharp. Still considered listenable for a 1970 AUD with decent instrument separation.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong early set with Black Peter and a high‑octane China>Rider>High Time, followed by an intense NFA → Drums → Good Lovin' → The Other One → NFA → Lovelight sequence; reviewers praise the seamless transitions and relentless energy despite tape cuts.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone on High Time praised as perfect; his vocal on Black Peter called emotional, and his fast, frenetic solo on The Other One highlighted.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s bass intro into Good Lovin' described as “machine‑gun” and a driving force that punches through the wall between sections.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s burning guitar work noted especially in the China > Rider transition; his rhythm playing praised throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s vocal performance lauded (especially on Black Peter and Good Lovin'); occasional organ solos absent but his showmanship acknowledged.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann’s drum segment described as tribal, “Zulu‑tribe” energy with powerful, stomping playing.
